insight: Recent rain (15 mm over the past few days) is washing urban runoff into the surf — the single biggest cause of beach contamination — especially near storm drains and creek mouths. The model's main signals right now: 15 mm of rain has fallen, washing bacteria-laden runoff into the surf; high tide timing is raising risk — how long before mid-morning the last high tide fell, which sets how much the water has just washed off the upper beach; and elevated river/creek flow is raising risk by carrying watershed runoff to the shore. There's no recent lab sample to anchor this (the last was 33 days ago), so the estimate is based entirely on current environmental conditions. It's a naturally clean, well-flushed open-coast beach (unsafe only ~3% of the time), so outside of storms it's reliably safe.
